top_story: Trump’s March threat to destroy Iran’s power grid unless Tehran reopened the Strait of Hormuz set an escalatory baseline, with Tehran signaling it would widen any confrontation across the region. By June 16, that posture had shifted into a narrow US-Iran understanding in favor of an immediate and permanent end to military operations in Lebanon, suggesting both sides now see containment as preferable to another open front. That diplomatic convergence remains fragile because Israel’s decision on whether to stop the Lebanon war is still unresolved, and Gaza underscores the cost of failed restraint: more than 1,000 people were killed during the cease-fire, including 121 women and 253 children. The regional picture is one of great-power deconfliction colliding with battlefield autonomy, leaving civilians to absorb the consequences where political control is weakest.
